whyWrong.en: VLANs separate Layer 2 broadcast domains; without VRFs the router still merges everything into one global routing table where the overlapping routes would collide.
whyWrong.hi: VLANs Layer 2 broadcast domains alag karte hain; VRFs ke bina router phir bhi sab kuch ek global routing table mein mila deta hai jahan overlapping routes takrayenge.

whyWrong.en: HSRP provides a redundant default gateway; it does nothing to separate routing tables.
whyWrong.hi: HSRP redundant default gateway deta hai; routing tables alag karne mein iska koi role nahi.

whyWrong.en: NAT translates addresses at a boundary but the router would still hold one routing table, so the overlapping internal routes would still conflict.
whyWrong.hi: NAT boundary par addresses translate karta hai lekin router mein phir bhi ek hi routing table hogi, isliye overlapping internal routes conflict karenge.

text.en: Enter the command that lists the VRF instances configured on a router together with their assigned interfaces.
text.hi: Woh command enter karo jo router par configured VRF instances ko unke assigned interfaces ke saath list karta hai.

explanation.en: show vrf displays each VRF name, its route distinguisher, supported protocols, and member interfaces — the first check when verifying that interfaces landed in the intended routing instance.
explanation.hi: show vrf har VRF ka naam, uska route distinguisher, supported protocols aur member interfaces dikhata hai — yeh verify karne ka pehla check ki interfaces sahi routing instance mein gaye hain.

text.en: A company subscribes to a provider-hosted email and office suite accessed through a web browser; the provider manages the servers, storage, and the application itself. Which cloud service model is this?
text.hi: Ek company provider-hosted email aur office suite subscribe karti hai jo web browser se access hota hai; servers, storage aur application khud provider manage karta hai. Yeh kaunsa cloud service model hai?

explanation.en: Software as a Service delivers a finished application over the network — the customer only consumes it, while the provider runs everything underneath. Hosted email suites are the textbook example.
explanation.hi: Software as a Service network par ek ready application deliver karta hai — customer sirf use karta hai, jabki neeche sab kuch provider chalata hai. Hosted email suites iska textbook example hain.

options.en: SaaS
options.hi: SaaS

options.en: IaaS
options.hi: IaaS

options.en: PaaS
options.hi: PaaS

options.en: Hybrid cloud
options.hi: Hybrid cloud

whyWrong.en: With IaaS the customer rents infrastructure (VMs, storage, networks) and must install and manage the OS and applications — not the case here.
whyWrong.hi: IaaS mein customer infrastructure (VMs, storage, networks) rent karta hai aur OS aur applications khud install aur manage karta hai — yahan aisa nahi hai.

whyWrong.en: With PaaS the customer deploys its own code onto a managed platform; here the application itself belongs to the provider.
whyWrong.hi: PaaS mein customer apna code managed platform par deploy karta hai; yahan application khud provider ki hai.

whyWrong.en: Hybrid cloud is a deployment model (private plus public combined), not a service model describing what is delivered.
whyWrong.hi: Hybrid cloud ek deployment model hai (private plus public combined), service model nahi jo batata hai ki kya deliver hota hai.

text.en: A development team wants to deploy its own application code while the provider manages the operating system, runtime, and underlying servers. Which cloud service model fits?
text.hi: Ek development team apna application code deploy karna chahti hai jabki provider operating system, runtime aur underlying servers manage kare. Kaunsa cloud service model fit hota hai?

explanation.en: Platform as a Service exposes a managed development and runtime platform: developers push code and the provider handles OS patching, runtime, scaling, and hardware. It sits between IaaS (more customer control) and SaaS (no customer code at all).
explanation.hi: Platform as a Service ek managed development aur runtime platform deta hai: developers code push karte hain aur provider OS patching, runtime, scaling aur hardware handle karta hai. Yeh IaaS (customer ka zyada control) aur SaaS (customer ka koi code nahi) ke beech mein aata hai.

options.en: PaaS
options.hi: PaaS

options.en: IaaS
options.hi: IaaS

options.en: SaaS
options.hi: SaaS

options.en: Private cloud
options.hi: Private cloud

whyWrong.en: With IaaS the team would receive raw VMs and have to manage the operating system and runtime themselves.
whyWrong.hi: IaaS mein team ko raw VMs milte aur operating system aur runtime khud manage karne padte.

whyWrong.en: SaaS delivers a finished third-party application; the team could not deploy its own code onto it.
whyWrong.hi: SaaS ek ready third-party application deta hai; team us par apna code deploy nahi kar sakti.

whyWrong.en: Private cloud describes who owns and uses the infrastructure (a deployment model), not the division of management duties.
whyWrong.hi: Private cloud batata hai ki infrastructure ka owner aur user kaun hai (deployment model), management duties ka batwara nahi.

text.en: Which two are essential characteristics of cloud computing as defined by NIST? (Choose two.)
text.hi: NIST ki definition ke hisaab se cloud computing ki kaunsi do essential characteristics hain? (Do chuno.)

explanation.en: NIST lists five essential characteristics: on-demand self-service, broad network access, resource pooling, rapid elasticity (capacity scales up and down with demand), and measured service (usage is metered and billed).
explanation.hi: NIST paanch essential characteristics list karta hai: on-demand self-service, broad network access, resource pooling, rapid elasticity (capacity demand ke saath upar-neeche scale hoti hai), aur measured service (usage meter hota hai aur bill hota hai).

options.en: Rapid elasticity
options.hi: Rapid elasticity

options.en: Measured service
options.hi: Measured service

options.en: Dedicated single-tenant hardware for every customer
options.hi: Har customer ke liye dedicated single-tenant hardware

options.en: Provisioning performed manually through provider support tickets
options.hi: Provider support tickets ke through manually kiya gaya provisioning

options.en: A guarantee that all data stays on the customer's premises
options.hi: Guarantee ki saara data customer ke premises par hi rahega

whyWrong.en: Clouds are built on resource pooling — multi-tenant infrastructure shared across customers — the opposite of mandatory single-tenant hardware.
whyWrong.hi: Clouds resource pooling par bante hain — customers ke beech shared multi-tenant infrastructure — jo mandatory single-tenant hardware ka ulta hai.

whyWrong.en: On-demand self-service means customers provision resources themselves through a portal or API, without waiting on tickets.
whyWrong.hi: On-demand self-service ka matlab hai customers portal ya API se khud resources provision karte hain, tickets ka wait kiye bina.

whyWrong.en: Data location depends on the deployment model; public cloud data lives in provider facilities, so this is not a defining characteristic.
whyWrong.hi: Data location deployment model par depend karti hai; public cloud data provider ki facilities mein rehta hai, isliye yeh defining characteristic nahi hai.

text.en: A company needs connectivity from its data center to a public cloud provider with predictable latency and bandwidth that never traverses the public internet. Which connection method meets the requirement?
text.hi: Ek company ko apne data center se public cloud provider tak aisi connectivity chahiye jismein latency aur bandwidth predictable ho aur jo kabhi public internet se na guzre. Kaunsa connection method yeh requirement poori karta hai?

explanation.en: Private interconnect offerings (such as a dedicated circuit or an MPLS provider cross-connect into the cloud edge) bypass the internet entirely, giving contracted bandwidth and consistent latency — the choice for latency-sensitive or high-volume hybrid workloads.
explanation.hi: Private interconnect offerings (jaise dedicated circuit ya cloud edge mein MPLS provider cross-connect) internet ko poori tarah bypass karte hain, contracted bandwidth aur consistent latency dete hain — latency-sensitive ya high-volume hybrid workloads ke liye yahi choice hai.

options.en: A dedicated private WAN circuit into the cloud provider's edge (private interconnect)
options.hi: Cloud provider ke edge tak dedicated private WAN circuit (private interconnect)

options.en: A site-to-site IPsec VPN across the internet
options.hi: Internet ke across site-to-site IPsec VPN

options.en: Accessing the cloud workloads over HTTPS
options.hi: Cloud workloads ko HTTPS par access karna

options.en: A GRE tunnel built over a broadband internet connection
options.hi: Broadband internet connection par bana GRE tunnel

whyWrong.en: IPsec encrypts the traffic, but the packets still ride the public internet, so latency and throughput remain unpredictable.
whyWrong.hi: IPsec traffic ko encrypt karta hai, lekin packets phir bhi public internet par chalte hain, isliye latency aur throughput unpredictable rehte hain.

whyWrong.en: HTTPS is just encrypted application access — still over the internet with no performance guarantees.
whyWrong.hi: HTTPS sirf encrypted application access hai — phir bhi internet par, bina kisi performance guarantee ke.

whyWrong.en: A GRE tunnel over broadband also transits the internet, and GRE adds no encryption either.
whyWrong.hi: Broadband par GRE tunnel bhi internet se guzarta hai, aur GRE koi encryption bhi add nahi karta.

text.en: Which set of 2.4 GHz channels is non-overlapping and recommended for adjacent access points (FCC domain)?
text.hi: 2.4 GHz channels ka kaunsa set non-overlapping hai aur adjacent access points ke liye recommended hai (FCC domain)?

explanation.en: 2.4 GHz channels are spaced only 5 MHz apart, but each transmission is about 22 MHz wide, so neighbors overlap heavily. Channels 1, 6, and 11 are far enough apart to avoid overlap, so adjacent APs alternate among them.
explanation.hi: 2.4 GHz channels sirf 5 MHz ki doori par hain, lekin har transmission lagbhag 22 MHz chauda hota hai, isliye paas wale channels bahut zyada overlap karte hain. Channels 1, 6 aur 11 itne door hain ki overlap nahi hota, isliye adjacent APs inhi mein alternate karte hain.

options.hi: 1, 5 aur 9
1, 2 aur 3

whyWrong.en: Channels 4 apart (1, 5, 9) still overlap with 22 MHz-wide signals; the accepted non-overlapping plan in the FCC domain is 1, 6, 11.
whyWrong.hi: 4 ki doori wale channels (1, 5, 9) 22 MHz-wide signals ke saath phir bhi overlap karte hain; FCC domain mein accepted non-overlapping plan 1, 6, 11 hai.

whyWrong.en: Channels 2, 7, and 12 overlap channels around them, and channel 12 is restricted in the FCC domain.
whyWrong.hi: Channels 2, 7 aur 12 apne aas-paas ke channels se overlap karte hain, aur FCC domain mein channel 12 restricted hai.

whyWrong.en: Adjacent channels 1, 2, and 3 overlap almost completely and would interfere severely.
whyWrong.hi: Adjacent channels 1, 2 aur 3 lagbhag poori tarah overlap karte hain aur bahut zyada interfere karenge.

text.en: Which 802.11 standard can operate in both the 2.4 GHz and 5 GHz bands?
text.hi: Kaunsa 802.11 standard 2.4 GHz aur 5 GHz dono bands mein operate kar sakta hai?

explanation.en: 802.11n (Wi-Fi 4) was the first standard to run in either band and introduced MIMO and channel bonding. (802.11ax, Wi-Fi 6, is also dual-band — and adds 6 GHz as Wi-Fi 6E — but it is not among these options.)
explanation.hi: 802.11n (Wi-Fi 4) pehla standard tha jo dono mein se kisi bhi band mein chal sakta tha, aur isne MIMO aur channel bonding introduce kiye. (802.11ax, Wi-Fi 6, bhi dual-band hai — aur Wi-Fi 6E ke roop mein 6 GHz add karta hai — lekin woh in options mein nahi hai.)

whyWrong.en: 802.11a operates only in the 5 GHz band (54 Mbps, OFDM).
whyWrong.hi: 802.11a sirf 5 GHz band mein operate karta hai (54 Mbps, OFDM).

whyWrong.en: 802.11b operates only in the 2.4 GHz band (11 Mbps, DSSS).
whyWrong.hi: 802.11b sirf 2.4 GHz band mein operate karta hai (11 Mbps, DSSS).

whyWrong.en: 802.11ac (Wi-Fi 5) operates only in the 5 GHz band.
whyWrong.hi: 802.11ac (Wi-Fi 5) sirf 5 GHz band mein operate karta hai.

text.en: Which two conditions commonly degrade performance on a 2.4 GHz WLAN? (Choose two.)
text.hi: Kaunsi do conditions aam taur par 2.4 GHz WLAN ki performance kharab karti hain? (Do chuno.)

explanation.en: The 2.4 GHz ISM band is crowded: microwave ovens, Bluetooth, cordless phones, and other non-Wi-Fi emitters all raise the noise floor. APs on channels that partially overlap create adjacent-channel interference — noise the radios cannot decode or defer to cleanly, which is worse than sharing the exact same channel.
explanation.hi: 2.4 GHz ISM band bahut bhara hua hai: microwave ovens, Bluetooth, cordless phones aur doosre non-Wi-Fi emitters sab noise floor badhate hain. Partially overlapping channels par chal rahe APs adjacent-channel interference create karte hain — aisa noise jise radios na theek se decode kar sakte hain na uske liye defer kar sakte hain, jo exact same channel share karne se bhi bura hai.

options.en: Interference from microwave ovens and Bluetooth devices sharing the band
options.hi: Band share karne wale microwave ovens aur Bluetooth devices se interference

options.en: Nearby access points operating on partially overlapping channels such as 3 and 6
options.hi: Paas ke access points jo 3 aur 6 jaise partially overlapping channels par chal rahe hon

options.en: Too many non-overlapping channels being available
options.hi: Bahut zyada non-overlapping channels available hona

options.en: Radar-triggered DFS channel changes
options.hi: Radar-triggered DFS channel changes

options.en: Using WPA2 with AES encryption
options.hi: AES encryption ke saath WPA2 use karna

whyWrong.en: The band's real problem is the opposite — only three non-overlapping channels exist, which forces reuse and co-channel contention.
whyWrong.hi: Band ki asli problem ulti hai — sirf teen non-overlapping channels hain, jisse reuse aur co-channel contention majboori ban jaata hai.

whyWrong.en: Dynamic frequency selection applies to certain 5 GHz channels shared with radar systems, not to the 2.4 GHz band.
whyWrong.hi: Dynamic frequency selection radar systems ke saath shared kuch 5 GHz channels par apply hota hai, 2.4 GHz band par nahi.

whyWrong.en: WPA2-AES encryption is performed in hardware and has no meaningful effect on RF performance.
whyWrong.hi: WPA2-AES encryption hardware mein hota hai aur RF performance par iska koi khaas asar nahi padta.

text.en: A wireless survey at a client location records a received signal strength of -65 dBm and a noise floor of -90 dBm. What is the signal-to-noise ratio?
text.hi: Ek client location par wireless survey -65 dBm received signal strength aur -90 dBm noise floor record karta hai. Signal-to-noise ratio kya hai?

explanation.en: SNR = signal minus noise: -65 - (-90) = 25 dB. Because both values are negative dBm, the signal being 'less negative' than the noise floor by 25 means it is 25 dB stronger. An SNR of 25 dB supports solid data rates; voice designs typically target 25 dB or better.
explanation.hi: SNR = signal minus noise: -65 - (-90) = 25 dB. Kyunki dono values negative dBm hain, signal ka noise floor se 25 'kam negative' hona matlab woh 25 dB zyada strong hai. 25 dB ka SNR achhe data rates support karta hai; voice designs aam taur par 25 dB ya usse better target karte hain.

options.en: 25 dB
options.hi: 25 dB

options.en: -25 dB
options.hi: -25 dB

options.en: 155 dB
options.hi: 155 dB

whyWrong.en: A negative SNR would mean the signal sits below the noise floor and is undecodable; here the signal is clearly above the noise.
whyWrong.hi: Negative SNR ka matlab hota ki signal noise floor se neeche hai aur decode nahi ho sakta; yahan signal saaf taur par noise se upar hai.

whyWrong.en: -155 comes from adding the two dBm figures; SNR is the difference between them, not the sum.
whyWrong.hi: -155 dono dBm figures ko jodne se aata hai; SNR inka difference hai, sum nahi.

whyWrong.en: 155 results from adding the magnitudes; subtract the noise floor from the signal level instead: -65 - (-90) = 25.
whyWrong.hi: 155 magnitudes ko jodne se aata hai; iski jagah signal level se noise floor subtract karo: -65 - (-90) = 25.
